keep: The idea is named in one line up front: the current is the steady value E ÷ R plus a gap that dies as a discharge does.
The steady state is found from the rule, by setting the rate to zero, so it is plain why L drops out of it and why the input alone sets it.

One worked example runs through every screen, computed from the shown rule: 24 V, 0.5 H and 10 Ω give 2.4 A, τ = 0.05 s, 48 A a second at switch-on, and gaps of −2.4, −0.883, −0.325 and −0.119 A at the τ marks.
The cause is drawn, not just the effect: rate arrows on screen 3 halve as the gap halves, which is why the gap obeys the decay rule of the discharge.

Each misconception in the brief has a puzzle and a drawn wrong pick: τ read as the time to full (screen 6), the start value not used (screen 8, 1.2(1 − e^(−t/0.05)) starts at 0), the steady line ignored (screens 8 and 13), L thought to set the final current (screen 10), and the fractions kept and closed swapped (screens 6 and 13).
Split shows the curve as the steady line plus the dying gap, so the general form i = E ÷ R + (i₀ − E ÷ R) e^(−t/τ) is seen before it is written.

The analogy, a cable warming to its running temperature under a steady load, reproduces the main result from his own work, and its break is true: several layers with different paces, and resistance that rises with temperature.
Practice has the safe way first, the steps, a rule of thumb, a worked example with fresh numbers, the integrating factor as a second route that lands on the same answer, and the mistakes.
fix: False absolute, in explain and whatAmILookingAt: 'the steady value never moves' is untrue once the supply is dropped mid-run on screens 8 and 9. Say it holds while the supply holds.
Causal step skipped in explain: 'Rearrange the rule as di/dt = (E ÷ R − i) ÷ (L ÷ R)' jumps two moves. Divide by L first, then take R out of the top.
Qualifier lost: the LibreTexts quote is about a driven damped system. Say a damped spring, not just a spring.
Brief names two causes: 'wherever the current starts' needs the start slider, which screen 5 lacks. Keep the one action, dragging the time marker.
Interactive shows the effect more than the cause on screen 5: add a rate arrow riding with the time marker, its slope the gap ÷ τ, so the shrinking gap is seen to slow its own closing.
Number rule: 'about 1300 rpm' and 'about 200 rpm' are not in numbers. Write the choices as the computed 1297 rpm and 203 rpm.
